data.spec_doc: docs/specs/genome-writes-stay-in-root.red-spec.json — FOUNDER RULING (Eugene, verbatim): "SLUGS ARE NOT IDENTIFIERS". The boundary is NOT a slug grammar: it is that no path the engine derives can ever leave the root it belongs to. A slug grammar may be added later as hygiene; no law here relies on one. THE HOLE (verified at e6c89ff): the file genome store, the genome writer, two readers and three appenders join a caller-supplied slug or gig id into a path with no check; path.join normalises `../`, so `../../x` writes outside the genome root, a skill slug `../..` creates directories and writes files outside it, agent_evolve reads agents/<slug>.json from wherever that lands and echoes the bytes back in next_def, gig_logs readdir()s and returns every .jsonl under gigs/<gig_id>, and output_write appends outputs/<gig_id>.jsonl wherever the gig id points. THE CONTRACT, for every site and every hostile value (../../x, ../.., a/../../x, an absolute path, a NUL byte, a backslash, and ../../g-sibling/x — a directory whose NAME shares the root's prefix, which a `startsWith(root)` check wrongly admits): (1) the call is REFUSED and the refusal names the boundary (matches /root/i); (2) nothing in the arena (root, root's parent, the prefix-sharing sibling) is created, modified or removed, byte-for-byte; (3) a refused genome write seals no ledger row — the check runs BEFORE #218's seal-before-write append; (4) for a read, a sentinel planted outside the root never appears in anything returned. A control per door: a normal slug still writes inside the root. The containment check must live in each WRITER, not only at a door: the blessed writers and the store port are driven directly, so a door-only check leaves those laws red. Sites NOT lawed, with why: charter_read (server.ts:2122) reads a caller-supplied PATH by design — not a derived path, a separate question for the founder; createCheckpointStore read/remove (reuse.ts:555-567) already refuse any gig id with a separator, and its write takes an engine-minted id; busPath (bus_terminal.ts:18) already refuses anything but a plain name; transcript_store (session ids from the runtime), reside_backing (randomUUID residency ids), local_queue and worker (engine-minted gig ids and directory listings), output_mirror metaFile (reached only through outputs.write, which the output_write law covers), and gig_dispatch's per-gig log dir (server.ts:1347/1564, keyed by resume_gig_id, which the checkpoint read already refuses when it carries a separator).
validation_criteria: FOUNDER RULING (Eugene, verbatim): "SLUGS ARE NOT IDENTIFIERS" — the boundary is that no path the engine derives can ever leave the root it belongs to, not a slug grammar; no law relies on a slug grammar
every site that derives a path from a caller's slug or gig id refuses a value whose path would leave its root, and the refusal names the root
a refused call changes nothing on disk anywhere in the arena, byte-for-byte (root, parent, prefix-sharing sibling)
a refused genome write seals no identity in the ledger
a read through a hostile value never returns bytes from outside the root
a normal slug still writes inside the root through every door (control)
each blessed writer and the store port hold the boundary themselves, not only the MCP doors
input_refs: founder ruling: SLUGS ARE NOT IDENTIFIERS
data.testing_method: vitest, example-based integration laws against the REAL call sites: the MCP tool surface (createToolSurface → callSurfaceTool → dispatchTool) for every door, local (genome_dir) and hosted (hosted:true over fileGenomeStore, no genome_dir); the exported writers/readers directly where no tool reaches them. Each law builds a fresh arena (base/d1/d2/g is the root, base/d1/d2/g-sibling a prefix-sharing sibling, nested so every hostile path lands INSIDE base and is observed rather than written into the host), snapshots every file (sha256) and directory under base before and after, and uses a MemoryLedger to prove no identity is sealed. Hostile values run as expect.soft so one run reports every value that gets through, not only the first. Plants were applied to a scratch prototype fix (not committed) one writer at a time, and each reddened exactly the laws named below; at e6c89ff every plant is applied at once, which is the observed RED: 25 laws red, 12 controls green.
